KnowledgeBundle.description: A self-contained, hierarchical collection of concept documents — the unit of distribution (a git repo, tarball, or subdirectory). Maps to a DCAT Catalog. When a whole bundle is serialized as a single JSON-LD document, this class is the tree root; individual concept files validate against Concept (or a subclass).

Concept.description: A single unit of knowledge within a bundle, represented as one markdown document. The abstract base of every LOKF type. Its own IRI (`id`) is the RDF subject; the markdown body and typed relations become triples about that subject.

Dataset.description: A collection of data, published or curated for access and reuse.

Table.description: A structured, tabular dataset (e.g. a warehouse table or view) whose columns are described by Field objects under `fields`.

Metric.description: A precisely defined, measurable quantity — the canonical definition of a business or operational metric.

Service.description: A callable service or API endpoint.

Playbook.description: A procedure or runbook — an ordered set of steps to accomplish a task or respond to an event. Serves the Diátaxis how-to (goal-oriented) mode.

Tutorial.description: A learning-oriented lesson: a guided, end-to-end practical activity through which a reader acquires a skill by doing. The Diátaxis tutorial mode as a first-class concept type; typically links to the reference and explanation it draws on with `references`.

Explanation.description: An understanding-oriented, discursive treatment of a topic that permits reflection. The Diátaxis explanation mode as a first-class concept type; typically links to its subject matter with `about`.

Policy.description: A governance, compliance, or operational policy document.

GlossaryTerm.description: A defined term in a controlled vocabulary or glossary. Maps to schema:DefinedTerm and skos:Concept.

Reference.description: A concept that mirrors an external source (a page, paper, or document) as a first-class citizen of the bundle so it can be cited and linked.

Document.description: A general knowledge document that does not fit a more specific type.

Role.description: A role an agent holds within an organization over a period of time — a job, appointment, or position. Reifies the agent–organization link so it can carry a title (roleName) and a start/end interval, following the schema.org Role and W3C ORG Membership patterns.

AttestedComputation.description: A sanctioned, immutable recipe for computing a value (OKF v0.2 §10), carried as its own concept type. The frontmatter is the contract: the agent may only bind the declared `parameters`, the `executor` runs the bound computation and returns a receipt, and the `attester` deterministically compares what actually ran against this recipe. The computation text lives in the body's `# Computation` fenced block or in the file named by `computation`. Semantically a prov:Plan with an attestation contract layered on.

Agent.description: A person or organization responsible for a concept.

Person.description: An individual person. Usable both as an inline Agent value (author, publisher) and as a standalone Concept document with a body and typed relations.

Organization.description: An organization, team, or group. Usable both as an inline Agent value (publisher) and as a standalone Concept document with a body and typed relations.

Field.description: A single column / property within a Table or Dataset schema. Maps to schema:PropertyValue.

Distribution.description: A specific accessible form of a Dataset (a file, feed, or endpoint). Maps to dcat:Distribution.

Relation.description: A typed, reified relationship from the containing concept to a target, used when a predicate is not covered by one of the named relation slots. Modeled as an rdf:Statement (subject = the containing concept).

Citation.description: A reference to an external source supporting a claim in a concept's body. Attached via the schema:citation predicate.
Citation.deprecated: Superseded in OKF v0.2 by Source (attached via `sources`). Remains functional for v0.1 documents.

Source.description: A material a concept derives from (OKF v0.2 §5.1) — a pointer (`resource`) plus objective per-source credibility signals (`author`, `usage_count`, `last_modified`) from which consumers infer trust; OKF stores signals, never a score. Markdown footnotes whose label equals `id` attribute individual claims to this entry. Supersedes Citation.

UsageWindow.description: The `{ from, to }` date range framing every `usage_count` signal (OKF v0.2 §5.1). Written once as a sibling of `sources`; a single Source entry MAY carry its own override.

Generation.description: How and when the current content was produced (OKF v0.2 `generated`, §5.2). Modeled as the PROV activity that generated the concept, so "who wrote this, when" is a one-hop join from the concept via prov:wasGeneratedBy, with both slots keeping PROV's activity-side semantics (prov:wasAssociatedWith, prov:endedAtTime) — domain/range correct with no reasoner or subproperty entailment required.

Verification.description: One verification event (OKF v0.2 `verified`, §5.2): an actor confirmed the content against its sources or resource at a time. Independent checks accumulate as separate events; trust tiers (unverified / machine-confirmed / human-reviewed) are derived from the actors, never stored. PROV has no Verification class, so the class IRI is honestly lokf-minted; the generated ontology declares it a subclass of prov:Activity.

Parameter.description: A typed, named hole in an Attested Computation that the agent may fill (OKF v0.2 §10.2). Binding semantics (SQL bind variable, dbt var, Python argument) follow the concept's `runtime`. The `type` key deliberately shares the global JSON-LD @type alias — see the attribute comment for the exact triple that results.

Executor.description: How an Attested Computation is run (OKF v0.2 §10.2): `resource` names run instructions or code a runner follows; `receipt` declares the field names a run must return — the evidence surface the attester inspects. No established vocabulary has an execution-interface class, so the IRI is honestly lokf-minted; schema:EntryPoint (an invocation specification) is the nearest real term.

Attester.description: The deterministic, non-LLM check for an Attested Computation (OKF v0.2 §10.2): `resource` names code that takes a run's receipt and returns a verdict, run consumer-side. Honestly lokf-minted.

id.description: The concept's stable IRI. By convention it is the bundle base IRI joined with the Concept ID (the file path within the bundle, minus the `.md` suffix). Becomes the JSON-LD @id / RDF subject.

type.description: The concept's type. OKF's single required field. In LOKF the value SHOULD name a LOKF class (e.g. Metric, Dataset, Table, Playbook, GlossaryTerm); it designates the JSON-LD @type / rdf:type. Consumers MUST tolerate unknown values by treating the concept as a generic lokf:Concept.

description.description: A single-sentence summary of the concept.

resource.description: A URI that uniquely identifies the underlying real-world asset the concept describes (a table console URL, an API base URL, etc.). Absent for purely abstract concepts.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 datetime of the last meaningful change.
timestamp.deprecated: Superseded in OKF v0.2 by `generated.at` (the `at` of the Generation event attached via `generated`). Remains functional; consumers MAY fall back to `timestamp` when `generated` is absent.

created.description: ISO 8601 datetime the concept was created.

version.description: A version string for the concept's content.

license.description: The license under which the concept or bundle is offered.

author.description: The agent(s) responsible for authoring the concept.

publisher.description: The agent responsible for making the bundle available.

body.description: The markdown body of the concept document (everything after the frontmatter). Mapped to schema:text; carried as a field only in the JSON-LD / JSON serialization, not duplicated in the frontmatter.

citations.description: External sources supporting claims in the body.
citations.deprecated: Superseded in OKF v0.2 by `sources`, which adds the stable `id` footnote-join key and per-source credibility signals (author, usage_count, last_modified). Remains functional; consumers SHOULD read `sources` and MAY still parse `citations` for v0.1 documents.

concepts.description: The concepts contained in a bundle.

relations.description: Typed relationships whose predicate is not covered by a named relation slot. Each entry is a reified Relation (predicate + target).

isPartOf.description: The target concept that this concept is a part of.

hasPart.description: A concept that is a part of this concept.

references.description: A concept or resource this concept refers to.

dependsOn.description: A concept this concept depends on.

derivedFrom.description: An entity this concept was derived from (provenance).

about.description: The subject matter this concept is about.

sameAs.description: An IRI asserting this concept is the same entity as another.

relatedTo.description: A generic association to another concept.

definedBy.description: A resource that formally defines this concept.

source.description: A resource from which this concept is derived or sourced.

genre.description: The Diátaxis documentation mode of the concept's markdown body (tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation). An optional facet that is orthogonal to `type`: `type` says what the concept is *about*, `genre` says how its prose *serves the reader*. Consumers MUST tolerate absent or unknown values.

predicate.description: The relationship type. SHOULD be drawn from the RelationType vocabulary.

target.description: The IRI (or Concept ID) of the relationship's object.

relation_label.description: An optional human-readable label for the relationship.

fields.description: The columns / properties that make up a dataset's schema.

datatype.description: The data type of a field.

unit.description: The unit of measurement (e.g. USD, seconds, count).

is_key.description: Whether the field is (part of) the primary key.

constraints.description: Free-text or expression describing constraints on a field.

access_url.description: A URL that gives access to a distribution.

media_type.description: The media (MIME) type of a distribution.

formula.description: The calculation or definition expression for a metric.

measures.description: What the metric measures (a concept IRI or description).

endpoint.description: The base URL or invocation endpoint of a service.

http_method.description: The HTTP method used to invoke the service, if applicable.

documentation.description: A link to the service's documentation.

definition.description: The formal definition of a term.

abbreviation.description: A short form or acronym for a term.

roleName.description: The name/title of the role held (e.g. a job title).

startDate.description: The date the role began (ISO 8601 date or year).

endDate.description: The date the role ended; omit for a role still held.

memberOf.description: The organization within which the role is held.

holder.description: The agent (typically a Person) who holds the role.

lokf_version.description: The LOKF version the bundle targets (e.g. "0.2").

okf_version.description: The OKF version the bundle remains compatible with (e.g. "0.2").

base_iri.description: The base IRI against which Concept IDs are resolved to produce each concept's stable `id`. Absolute http(s), ending in `/` or `#` so that ids mint by plain concatenation and prefix routing respects segment boundaries (`…/team/` never captures `…/team-archive/`).

context.description: The URL of the JSON-LD @context to attach to this bundle's concepts to interpret their frontmatter as Linked Data.

sources.description: The materials this concept derives from, each carrying objective credibility signals. Markdown footnotes join to entries via `sources[].id`. Supersedes `citations` and the body `# Citations` convention.

usage_window.description: The `{ from, to }` date range framing every `usage_count`. Attached both to Concept (the shared window, sibling of `sources`) and to Source (a per-entry override).

from.description: Start date (inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD) of a usage window.

to.description: End date (inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD) of a usage window.

usage_count.description: How often the source's resource was exercised (views, executions, reads) over the governing usage_window. An adoption/liveness signal read as order-of-magnitude and trend, not a score. Minted in lokf: no established vocabulary has a bare-integer usage property (schema:userInteractionCount is domained to the InteractionCounter reification).

last_modified.description: When the SOURCE itself last changed (YYYY-MM-DD). A recency signal about the source, distinct from `generated.at`, which records when this concept's content was produced. Same predicate as the deprecated `timestamp`, on a different subject node (source vs concept).

generated.description: How and when the current content was produced: `by` (REQUIRED actor) and `at` (ISO 8601 datetime). Supersedes the v0.1 `timestamp` field; consumers MAY fall back to `timestamp` when `generated` is absent.

verified.description: Verification events confirming the content against its sources or resource. Independent of `generated`: who wrote a concept need not be who confirmed it. Trust tiers derive from the actors: absent = unverified; only non-human actors = machine-confirmed; any `human:<id>` actor = human-reviewed. A bare `{ by, at }` mapping MUST be read as a one-element list; the LOKF loader normalizes the bare form before LinkML validation. Minted in lokf: no established vocabulary has an entity-to-verification-event property.

by.description: The actor that performed the event, as a plain OKF §7 actor string (`<producer>/<version>`, `human:<id>`, `process:<id>`) — a literal, never an IRI. Trust tiers derive from the `human:` prefix via string inspection (SPARQL STRSTARTS).

at.description: ISO 8601 datetime at which the event completed.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the concept: draft | stable | deprecated. Absent means stable (consumer-side default; absence is deliberately distinguishable from an explicit `status: stable`, so no ifabsent). Advisory, never access control.

stale_after.description: Absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD) on or after which the concept is stale (stale when today >= stale_after). schema:expires is the exact concept — a planned future expiry; prov:invalidatedAtTime would falsely assert the entity WAS invalidated, and dcterms:valid names a validity period only ambiguously.

runtime.description: REQUIRED on an Attested Computation. How to run the computation (bigquery | postgres | dbt | python | Looker | ...); defines what `parameters` mean and how the executor and attester interpret the contract.

parameters.description: The typed, named holes the agent may fill — the ONLY surface the agent may bind. Binding semantics follow `runtime`. Minted in lokf, mirroring the existing `fields` -> lokf:field idiom: schema.org attaches PropertyValueSpecifications only through the Actions -input/-output annotation syntax, which is not a reusable property.

required.description: Whether a value for the parameter must be supplied.

computation.description: Optional path to a file holding the computation; absent means the body's `# Computation` fenced block IS the computation. Minted in lokf: schema:contentUrl is the nearest real property but is scoped to MediaObject bytes.

executor.description: How the computation is run and what evidence a run must return.

receipt.description: The field names a run must return (e.g. job_id, executed_sql, result) — the evidence the attester inspects. Receipts themselves are runtime artifacts, never stored in the bundle. Minted in lokf: no established vocabulary describes a receipt-shape declaration.

attester.description: The deterministic, non-LLM verdict check over a receipt.

DiataxisMode.description: Learning-oriented; a lesson that lets a beginner acquire a skill by doing.
Goal-oriented; directions that guide an already-competent reader through a problem or towards a result.
Information-oriented; austere, authoritative description of the machinery.
Understanding-oriented; discursive treatment of a subject, that permits reflection and deepens comprehension.

ConceptStatus.description: Kept for links and history; no longer current.

HttpMethod.description: Retrieve a representation of the resource.
Submit data to be processed, often creating a resource.
Replace the resource with the supplied representation.
Apply a partial modification to the resource.
Like GET, but returns headers only, no body.
Describe the communication options for the resource.

deprecations.Citation: Superseded in OKF v0.2 by Source (attached via `sources`). Remains functional for v0.1 documents.
deprecations.timestamp: Superseded in OKF v0.2 by `generated.at` (the `at` of the Generation event attached via `generated`). Remains functional; consumers MAY fall back to `timestamp` when `generated` is absent.
deprecations.citations: Superseded in OKF v0.2 by `sources`, which adds the stable `id` footnote-join key and per-source credibility signals (author, usage_count, last_modified). Remains functional; consumers SHOULD read `sources` and MAY still parse `citations` for v0.1 documents.
